title: dbt-exasol
tagline: Build, test and document SQL models with dbt.
role: The dbt adapter for Exasol. dbt turns a folder of SELECT statements into managed tables and views with dependencies, tests and documentation; this add-on is what lets it speak to the kit's local database. Installing it is also what puts dbt itself on the machine - dbt-core comes with the adapter.
profile: The kit generates ~/.exasol-starter-kit/dbt/profiles.yml with a profile named exasol_starter_kit, and the launcher points dbt at that directory with DBT_PROFILES_DIR. Your own ~/.dbt/profiles.yml is never read or written - if you keep your warehouses in one file, copy the block out of the kit's copy rather than expecting the kit to merge into yours.
credentials: The password is never written into the profile. It names DBT_ENV_SECRET_EXASOL_PASSWORD, which the launcher fills from the kit's credential file at run time; dbt scrubs values under that prefix from its own logs and artifacts. The profile uses the runtime ADMIN user, not the read-only one the MCP server and dash-server share, because building models means creating tables.
installed_by: Never by the installer. Only through exakit marketplace.
platforms: macOS, Linux (including WSL) and Windows. Requires Python 3.11 to 3.14; the kit's managed interpreter (3.12) is inside that range, so nothing extra is needed.

quickstart.note: Space selects dbt-exasol, Enter installs it. That is the whole install - the profile and the launcher are written for you.

quickstart.step: Check it can reach the database
quickstart.note: Run it inside a dbt project. The install already ran this check for you if the database was up.
From a project folder. Models land in the DBT schema, which dbt creates on the first run.

notes: The command is `dbt-exasol`, not `dbt`. A dbt you installed yourself for another warehouse keeps that name - the kit does not take over a command it did not create.
dbt needs a project. `dbt-exasol run` outside a folder with a dbt_project.yml will tell you so; that is dbt's own behaviour, not a broken install.
Set `profile: exasol_starter_kit` in your dbt_project.yml to use the generated profile, or export your own DBT_PROFILES_DIR to use yours instead.

Models build into the DBT schema by default. dbt creates it on the first run; change it with the schema key in the generated profile, which `exakit update dbt-exasol` will then rewrite - so change it in your project's config if you want it to stick.

The generated profile sets validate_server_certificate: false, because the kit's local runtime speaks TLS with a self-signed certificate. That is correct here and wrong for a production warehouse - do not copy the block to one.
Uninstall removes the venv, the launcher and the generated profiles.yml. Anything else you put in ~/.exasol-starter-kit/dbt is left alone, including a project you kept there.

troubleshooting.symptom: Env var required but not provided: DBT_ENV_SECRET_EXASOL_PASSWORD
The marketplace does not list dbt-exasol

environment.name: DBT_PROFILES_DIR
environment.effect: Kit launcher supplies its private dbt profile directory when unset. Set your own directory to use a profile you manage.

environment.name: EXAKIT_DBT_EXASOL_VERSION
environment.effect: Override the tested adapter version for install/update.
